open_risks: C1 VERIFIED: sort -o, uniq IN OUT, xxd IN OUT, tree -o, yq -i all write under the root and classify ALLOW. Decision C's premise that these are flag-free stream filters is factually false.
C2 VERIFIED: sed carries write (w, s///w) and execute (GNU e) in the SCRIPT BODY, which sedAllows never inspects. Option-parsing sed is a losing parser race.

C3 VERIFIED: git clearance stops at the subcommand. git diff --output= writes; -c plus -p (BOTH on the approved global lists) gives arbitrary execution via core.pager; --exec-path and --config-env are the same class.

C4 VERIFIED: the 16 KB gate fails OPEN for relative paths - oversized absolute denies, oversized relative allows, same command under the cap denies. Decision G's justification for the residual is wrong whenever the root sits inside the project, the normal layout.
H5 VERIFIED: a FAILED cd and a SUBSHELL cd both move the guard's tracked cwd while the real shell stays in the root.

H6 VERIFIED: tracked cwd resets to projectDir every invocation while the Bash tool's shell PERSISTS cwd across calls, so cd ROOT in call 1 then a bare relative destructive command in call 2 allows. Needs no exotic syntax.
H7: isUnderRoot is lexical only, so a symlinked path component aliases past BOTH the Bash guard and the Write/Edit branch. The ONLY finding fixable without touching a locked artifact.
M8: an ancestor of the root is out of scope; under the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA layout rm -rf dataRoot destroys EVERY project's ledger, broader than the tracked worktree exclusion.
L9: roots are re-resolved by a git subprocess on every guarded call inside a 10s hook budget, so the deferred empty-roots bypass is reachable transiently from a git hiccup.
